summary: Paraguayan general Alfredo Stroessner seized power in a 1954 coup and ruled for 35 years through a US-backed police state that tortured dissidents, sheltered Nazi fugitives, handed land to cronies and procured young girls for him.

evidence.note: Solano Lopez takes power in 1862 and builds the army that he throws into the 1864 war
Stroessner introduced as a Chaco War mortar commander; German father, Paraguayan mother
1947 civil war won with his artillery, then a string of coups he joins before his own
his own coup in 1954 begins the 35-year regime
US aid rises after the coup; American advisers train his police in torture
segment on Forster's failed antisemitic colony, continued at the start of part 2
Paraguay as a refuge and smuggling base for Nazi fugitives, with Rudel and Mengele
Pastor Coronel runs the secret police; long section on torture and FBI ties
dissident doctors flee to Brazil and Argentina and are abducted under Condor
land concentration, ill-gotten lands given to generals, smuggling as patronage
extended account of girls procured and abused for the dictator
1989 coup by his son-in-law; exile in Brazil until his death at 93

notes: Transcript dates Forster's suicide to 1899 (sources say 1889) and the opening of the police archives to 1977 (actually 1992); lifespan follows the transcript per the rules. Coronel's death year is from my own knowledge. Covered span starts at Solano Lopez's rule; the 1811 Francia material is short background. Scope national though the wars and Condor cross borders.
